title: U.S. NCTC Formally Names 'El 03' as CJNG Leader; Discloses Triad Command Structure With El Chorro and El Sapo as Lieutenants
detail: The U.S. National Counterterrorism Center (NCTC) formally identified Juan Carlos Valencia González, alias 'El 03,' as CJNG's supreme leader following El Mencho's February 22 killing — the first official U.S. government confirmation of the succession, following the April 6 El País media report. The U.S. State Department reiterated its existing $5 million reward (in place since 2021 under a 2020 D.C. federal indictment for international drug trafficking and weapons charges) for information leading to his arrest. Valencia González, born September 12, 1984 in Santa Ana, California, is a dual U.S.-Mexican citizen and stepson of El Mencho via his mother Rosalinda González Valencia. NCTC's disclosure also named a formal two-lieutenant command structure beneath El 03: Julio Alberto Castillo Rodríguez ('El Chorro') — El Mencho's son-in-law, who controls Manzanillo port operations in Colima and CJNG's precursor-chemical supply chain, effectively resolving the 29+ day Manzanillo plaza-boss command void that followed El Chucky's May 9 arrest — and Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán ('El Sapo'), CJNG's military chief. The disclosure recasts the previously reported 'El 03 vs. El Sapo' succession binary as a consolidated triad rather than a rivalry, though independent confirmation of the internal hierarchy's stability remains pending. El Jardinero (Audias Flores Silva), arrested April 27, was noted as a fourth senior figure now sidelined by detention.

title: La Nueva Familia Michoacana Drone-Bombs Guajes de Ayala, Guerrero, as World Cup Diverts Security Forces
detail: Cartel drones began dropping explosives on the Guajes de Ayala cluster of rural communities in Guerrero at approximately 6 a.m. Wednesday, July 8, 2026, as La Nueva Familia Michoacana — designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization by the Trump administration in 2025 — escalated its encroachment on the self-defense communities first documented in March 2026. Roughly 70 women, children, and elderly residents sheltered in an abandoned medical clinic as drone explosions and gunfire continued between cartel operatives and the community's vigilante group. Residents said their weeks of warnings to Guerrero state authorities went unheeded because military, National Guard, and police assets had been redeployed to fortify Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey for the FIFA World Cup, leaving non-host regions comparatively exposed. Security analyst David Saucedo assessed the redeployment as having created tactical voids exploited by cartels operating outside CJNG's own tournament-window blackout directive. The incident illustrates the broader post-Mencho fragmentation dynamic — regional and rival cartels expanding into contested ground during CJNG's decapitation-driven recalibration — even though La Nueva Familia Michoacana is not itself a CJNG faction.
